q1_issues.issue: (Century 16) uses a time-term granularity the instruction set does not define; the licensed structured terms are Year / Month / Day / Weekday / Hour / Minute only, and no bounded form is offered for a century either.
The per-member capture rule carries only Past and omits the Time atom the group event has, so a capture distributed to an individual city has no time.

q2_gaps: century- and decade-scale time expressions ('in the 16th century'): no term constructor exists at that granularity and no rule says to convert it into Year bounds

per-member distribution over an OBJECT-side group; the distributive-rule machinery is specified for a plural subject ('each member acts separately'), leaving the object-group case ('captured many cities') unstated
notes: The algerian_city fusion plus its genus riding in the group's kind slot matches the breton_tapestry plural pattern exactly, and Theme for 'captured' and Agent for the inanimate transitive subject both follow the tests. CardinalityPhrase "many" is borderline: 'many' is listed among the proportion words that set strength and is absent from the vague-quantity phrase list, though the 'counts things' test does point this way here.
